context.observation_scope: PADDOCK Issues work: finite-state model-test adjustment, PostgreSQL DDL preparation, static checks, and attempted operator-provided database URL workflow.

answers.ambiguous: The overall request was clear. I treated setting PADDOCK_DB_URL as authorization to attempt the requested DB validation, but checked for the client first; no connection or SQL execution occurred because psql is absent.
answers.excessive: No clearly unnecessary instruction or skill step was observed in this task.
answers.hard-to-operate: The runtime lacks psql, so a configured PADDOCK_DB_URL alone cannot be used to verify the database or apply sql/init.sql. This forced stopping before DB checks; installing tools was not authorized.
answers.helpful: Keeping the database target constrained to paddock_test and the DDL schema-qualified under raw, preserving unrelated working-tree changes, and separating static validation from unverified database execution helped avoid unsafe claims or writes.
answers.missing: A preinstalled PostgreSQL client or an approved, secret-safe database validation mechanism that can run a specified SQL file and report only version, target database, and exit status.
answers.next-time: Check client availability before preparing a DB run, then verify the database identity/version without exposing the URL and only then apply the SQL. If no client exists, stop and give the operator a minimal safe command to run elsewhere.
answers.other: Observation by the assistant during task execution; these are not user-authored survey answers. No database operation was performed.
